questions.q: The roots of a polynomial equation are 0, 2, and $-5$. Which of the following is a factored form of the equation?
questions.explain: If a polynomial has roots $r_1, r_2,$ and $r_3$, its factors include $(x - r_1)$, $(x - r_2)$, and $(x - r_3)$. Substituting the given roots 0, 2, and $-5$ gives the factors $(x - 0)$, $(x - 2)$, and $(x - (-5))$. This simplifies to $x$, $(x - 2)$, and $(x + 5)$. Setting their product to zero yields the equation $x(x - 2)(x + 5) = 0$.
questions.subject: Mathematics
